open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence identity across restore
open_points.text: “one more than the last its store ever wrote; never reused in that store” contradicts “A store the owner restores from a backup continues from the backup's last number” when the store wrote later entries before being restored.
open_points.question: After restoring a backup, is this the same store, requiring the sequence to continue above every number written before the restore, or a new store incarnation allowed to reuse numbers lost by the restore?
options: The restored store retains its identity and never reuses any pre-restore sequence number
A restore creates a new store incarnation whose numbering resumes from the backup
Sequence numbers may be reused after restore without a store-incarnation identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored store as the same store and persist a high-water mark outside rollback so no sequence number is reused.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry lifecycle under backup restore
open_points.text: “the entries written after the backup are lost with it and exist nowhere” adds a second removal path, while M09 still says “Only the owner erases it, by date”, gives the lifecycle only as “written -> erased by the owner's dated erasure”, and State 0 says that erasure leaves an entry of its own.
open_points.question: Does restoring a backup legitimately remove AuditEntries without the dated audit-erasure action and without recording an erasure entry, and if so is backup loss part of the AuditEntry lifecycle?
options: Restore loss is an explicit second lifecycle transition with no erasure entry
Restore must preserve or reconstruct all later AuditEntries
Restore loss is treated as the existing dated erasure action
open_points.default_guess: Add restore loss as an explicit second lifecycle transition, since the new text expressly says those entries cease to exist.

open_points.subject: Backup check that protects MigrationClosure
open_points.text: “once one holding the closure has passed its check” does not identify the check, who performs it, which action reads the MigrationClosure, or what event causes pre-import backups to stop being kept.
open_points.question: What product or administrative action checks a backup containing the MigrationClosure, and does successful completion of that action trigger deletion of every pre-import backup?
options: A backup-verification action reads the closure and then removes pre-import backups
A tested-restore action reads the closure and then removes pre-import backups
The import itself removes all pre-import backups
Backup retention is external and no Registry action reads the closure for this purpose
open_points.default_guess: A backup-verification action confirms that the closure is present and restorable, after which the owner removes all pre-import backups.
